title: A simulated interview is a hypothesis machine
goal: Use a fictional persona to generate questions for real research, not fake validation.
explanation: A language model’s persona reflects learned stereotypes and your prompt. It does not represent actual customers or their subconscious reactions. Define situational needs instead of demographic caricatures, then convert the simulated objections into neutral questions for consented real interviews.
sampleInput: Idea: a kitchen inventory app that suggests meals. Fictional situation: someone has ten minutes to cook, shares a kitchen, dislikes repetitive data entry and uses an older phone. No actual customer interview has happened.
prompt: Simulate a skeptical potential user with the stated constraints, without inventing a real identity. Give five possible objections, label them hypotheses, and turn each into a non-leading interview question. Do not claim purchase intent, demographic representativeness or research findings.
workedExample: Hypothesis: entering every ingredient may take too long. Neutral question: “How do you currently keep track of ingredients, if at all?” Leading question to reject: “Wouldn’t automatic inventory save you lots of time?”

steps.title: Describe the situation
steps.text: Use tasks, constraints and current behaviour rather than age/gender stereotypes.

steps.title: Generate hypotheses
steps.text: Request five objections with the explicit simulated label.

steps.title: Convert to questions
steps.text: Rewrite each objection into a question that does not suggest the desired answer.

steps.title: Spot invented validation
steps.text: Remove claims such as “users will love it” or a fabricated willingness-to-pay number.

steps.title: Plan real research
steps.text: Write a consented interview plan, recruitment limits and what would disconfirm the idea.

checks: All simulated responses are labelled hypotheses, not customer quotes.
Interview questions avoid selling the idea or implying the answer.
The plan includes real consented research and a disconfirming observation.
commonMistakes: Reporting a model’s persona output as market validation.
Using stereotyped demographics as a substitute for actual needs.
offline: Brainstorm objections yourself and turn them into neutral questions; no simulated participants are needed.
reflection: What observation from a real person would contradict the most attractive simulation result?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All simulated responses are labelled hypotheses, not customer quotes.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Interview questions avoid selling the idea or implying the answer.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Reporting a model’s persona output as market validation.
